claims.text: The studied material is a nominally equiatomic AlCrCoFeNi high-entropy alloy.
The initial alloy contains approximately 79% BCC and 21% ordered B2 phases.
The initial alloy has a maze-like, spinodally decomposed microstructure.
EDS measures approximately 17.26 at.% Al in the initial alloy.
Protective-oxide development and retention in this alloy are governed by selective oxidation of Al.
In air at high temperature, Al diffuses outward much more rapidly than the other alloying elements.
Outwardly transported Al reacts with oxygen to form a continuous external Al2O3 layer.
A Cr2O3-rich inner region forms beneath the external Al2O3 layer, producing a duplex oxide scale.
The alumina scale and Cr-rich inner layer limit oxygen ingress and thereby slow further oxidation.
Selective Al oxidation causes localized subsurface Al depletion.
Localized Al depletion drives transformation of the initial BCC/B2 matrix through FCC and Cr-Fe-rich sigma phases.
Low oxygen pressure limits Al outward transport and produces a thinner, predominantly alumina film.
The thinner oxide formed under vacuum causes less pronounced subsurface phase transformation than exposure in air.
Air treatment will cause oxidation to begin earlier and become more extensive than vacuum treatment.
Air treatment will produce a thicker duplex oxide scale than vacuum treatment.
Air treatment will produce more pronounced Al depletion and subsurface FCC and transient sigma formation than vacuum treatment.
FCC formation begins at approximately 550 °C, sigma formation at approximately 600–650 °C, and pronounced oxidation at approximately 900–1000 °C.
The proposed behavior applies to arc-melted AlCrCoFeNi heated to no more than 1100 °C under air or vacuum with oxygen partial pressure around 8.82×10^-7 atm.
